Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{BA}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{FA}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{FE}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{CE}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{CB}$ in terms of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$ To denote the corresponding vectors, use $a$, $b,$ $c,$ and $d.$

$\overset{\to }{CB}=$   
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $C$ to $B$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{CB}=\overset{\to }{CE}+\overset{\to }{EF}+\overset{\to }{FA}+\overset{\to }{AB}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/18b8d39937dd23f03a030727e642729259ec5ab0c6fcb438c8bf82a2b7aaf08d.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{CE}=d,\,\overset{\to }{EF}=-c,\,\overset{\to }{FA}=b,\,\overset{\to }{AB}=-a.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/6f1c084747ad1b0de2ab28979fee8e14db9463f1d82d07ab787581789bcb6e37.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{CB} & =\overset{\to }{CE}+\overset{\to }{EF}+\overset{\to }{FA}+\overset{\to }{AB} \\  & =d-c+b-a.\end{aligned}
$$
